Article Title: Jharkhand protest: BJP bandh, ED probe, arrests deepen recruitment exam row - top developments
Article Text:
The BJP has called a statewide bandh in Jharkhand to protest alleged police force against students.

BJP calls bandh over police action

Students allege brutal crackdown

ED launches money laundering probe

Students demand CBI investigation

Hunger strike leader's health worsens

Soren seeks dialogue amid political row

NEW DELHI: Normal life was affected in parts of Jharkhand on Tuesday as the BJP enforced a statewide bandh over police action against job aspirants during their march to the state assembly, while an Enforcement Directorate probe and the arrest of a former JPSC chairperson added a new dimension to the recruitment exam controversy.Most schools and business establishments remained closed, while vehicular movement was thin in Ranchi and several other cities. The bandh, announced from 8 am to midnight, was called by the BJP to protest the use of water cannons, tear gas and batons against students during Monday's assembly march. Essential services were kept outside its purview.BJP state president Aditya Sahu described the police action as "atrocities" against students and accused the JMM-led government of using force instead of addressing their grievances. The party has backed demands for an independent probe into alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad has also condemned the alleged police action and announced a 'Vidhan Sabha March' from the old assembly building to the new assembly premises.The bandh followed a tense day in Ranchi when thousands of aspirants breached multiple barricades while marching towards the assembly, where the monsoon session was underway.Police used water cannons and tear gas near Jagannathpur Temple before resorting to a lathi-charge after protesters crossed the final barricade and reached Gate No 1.Student leaders alleged that the protest was peaceful until police action began in the evening. Ravinder Pasawan said students from all 24 districts had gathered and waited until 5 pm for the government to respond to their demands."But suddenly, force was used. Some of our companions were injured. The administration did its job; before that, they were quite cooperative, but in the evening, they lost their cool. Many of our colleagues, including women students, were injured. It was also seen that media personnel were pushed and shoved. We remain firm on our demands. We appeal to the Honourable Chief Minister that we are all students; please accept our demands, as they are all logical. Our indefinite protest will continue until the Jharkhand government accepts them," Pasawan said.Another student leader, Piyush, claimed nearly 50,000 aspirants had participated in what he described as a "historic" march. He said the students remained independent of political parties and would continue their indefinite protest.Police, however, said 14 personnel were injured during the protests and that CCTV footage would be examined to identify those involved in stone pelting and disruption.The controversy escalated further on Monday after the Enforcement Directorate launched a money laundering investigation into alleged irregularities in multiple recruitment examinations, particularly the JSSC-CGL examination.The Jharkhand CID also arrested former JPSC chairperson L Khiangte in connection with the alleged irregularities. His arrest took the number of people apprehended in the case to 20.Khiangte, a 1988-batch IAS officer and former Jharkhand chief secretary, was appointed JPSC chairperson in February last year and resigned on July 22. The CID had earlier searched 18 locations across Ranchi, Palamu, Hazaribagh, Bokaro and Dhanbad.The state government has agreed to cancel the 14th JPSC examination and backlog examinations conducted in 2023 and 2025. Higher and Technical Education Minister Sudivya Kumar said the government had also agreed to the ED probe after evidence of financial irregularities emerged.The protesters have been agitating since July 25, demanding cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination, a CBI probe into alleged irregularities and comprehensive reforms in the JPSC and JSSC.They have also sought cancellation of several recruitment examinations, including the 14th Jharkhand PSC Civil Services Examination, and an independent investigation either by the CBI or a panel of retired high court judges from outside Jharkhand.On the JSSC-CGL examination, Kumar said the state government could not order its cancellation because it was conducted under court monitoring. The government has proposed a committee headed by a retired high court judge to oversee the CID investigation, but protesters have rejected the proposal.The government has also proposed reforms to the standard operating procedures of the JPSC and JSSC, with inputs from IIT-ISM Dhanbad, IIM-Ranchi and XLRI Jamshedpur.JLKM leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who has been on hunger strike for nine days over the issue, was admitted to Ranchi Sadar Hospital after his blood sugar level dropped "drastically". Doctors described his condition as critical.Mahto joined Monday's march in an ambulance and later addressed protesters while lying on a stretcher. His supporters alleged that he was injured during the police action.Earlier, Mahto had said, "Attempts were made to stop us. Barricades of barbed wire were erected. Water cannons were used. Tear gas was deployed. Lathi charges were carried out, leaving people injured. Yet, we did not raise a single slogan against the government. We did not engage in any political rhetoric or utter a single obscene word. The only flag present was the Tricolour."He also questioned the credibility of any investigation, saying, "Exams are conducted with candidates sitting in places like Nepal. What faith can one have in the investigation?"Chief minister Hemant Soren urged students to resolve their grievances through "dialogue and trust", while saying their demands would be examined with "utmost seriousness and sensitivity".Soren also accused opposition leaders of attempting to mislead students for political gains and said the government wanted to make the examination system more transparent, technology-enabled, secure and accountable.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi condemned the police action, saying peaceful protests should not be met with violence."Students have a right to peaceful protest, and only dialogue can yield solutions," the Congress leader said, urging the Jharkhand government to resolve their grievances at the earliest.His remarks drew a response from the BJP, which accused Gandhi of double standards because the Congress is part of the JMM-led ruling coalition in Jharkhand.
Article Summary: BJP has called a statewide bandh in Jharkhand to protest alleged police force against students. The party has backed demands for an independent probe into alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. The bandh followed a tense day in Ranchi when thousands of aspirants breached multiple barricades while marching towards the assembly.

Article Title: 'Images disturb me deeply': Congress' Sam Pitroda questions 'use of force' against Jharkhand students
Article Text:
Sam Pitroda backs Jharkhand student protests

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Sam Pitroda on Monday backed protesting students in Jharkhand as an agitation over alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC recruitment examinations intensified in Ranchi. Criticising the government’s use of lathis, tear gas and water cannons, Pitroda called for “reform, accountability and compassion” as the protests entered their 18th day.The development comes as the Jharkhand students’ 'Vidhan Sabha gherao' march in Ranchi on Monday saw police use lathis and water cannons to disperse protesters. The march was organised over alleged irregularities in examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).The protesters are demanding, among other measures, the cancellation of the JSSC-Combined Graduate Level (CGL) examination, a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into alleged irregularities and reforms in the recruitment process.In a series of posts on X, the Indian Overseas Congress (IOC) global chairman said the grievances of young people should be addressed through dialogue."The images from Ranchi disturb me deeply”, he wrote.Pitroda said students should not be met with force, calling them India's future and expressing solidarity with Jharkhand's youth.In another post, Pitroda said, "Democracy requires governments to create space for peaceful dissent, dialogue and resolution."Pitroda's remarks came after Congress leader Rahul Gandhi also condemned the police action and called for dialogue with the protesting students, urging the Jharkhand government to address their grievances. The Hemant Soren-led Jharkhand government is run by a JMM-led coalition in which the Congress is a partner.Pitroda also said the protesting youth deserved to be heard respectfully and urged authorities to address their concerns over fair examinations, transparent recruitment, employment opportunities and their prospects for the future."These are not unreasonable demands. India owes its youth a system they can trust”, he added in the postHe further said the concerns of students needed to be viewed in the context of the sacrifices made by their families."Behind every protesting student is a family that has sacrificed - often for years for education and the hope of a job.Pitroda criticised the JMM-led Jharkhand government over the handling of recruitment and examination-related grievances, saying delays in recruitment and failures in examinations risk eroding young people's trust in the system. He called for "reform, accountability and compassion" in addressing their concerns.Calling India's youth its "greatest assets", Pitroda said the country's demographic dividend could turn into frustration if education does not translate into opportunities and examinations fail to inspire confidence."We must redesign education, assessment and employment systems for this generation — not punish them for demanding change," he said.On Monday, police and protesters clashed during the march outside the Jharkhand Assembly. Police resorted to at least three rounds of lathicharge, while tear gas shells and water cannons were also used to disperse demonstrators.Injured protester alleged that police began the lathicharge without warning.The police have, however, given a different account of the events. Ranchi deputy commissioner Manjunath Bhajantri said a stone was thrown at a police jawan and alleged that some "anti-social elements" attempted to provoke police and officials during the protest.Addressing a press conference, Bhajantri said the police had exercised restraint throughout the demonstration and used "mild force" only after a situation arose in which a jawan's life was allegedly at risk.Ranchi City SP Paras Rana said most students were peaceful but alleged that a section of protesters damaged barricades and pelted stones.The protest also affected Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM) leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who was admitted to Sadar Hospital in Ranchi after taking part in the march.Mahto had been on hunger strike for nine days at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium before joining the 'Vidhan Sabha Gherao' march despite his deteriorating health. He was later admitted to hospital.The police action drew criticism from political leaders across party lines. On Monday, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi also condemned the police action and called for dialogue with the protesting students."The use of force against students protesting in Jharkhand is wrong. Students have a right to peaceful protest, and only dialogue can yield solutions," Rahul Gandhi said in a post on X, on Monday.He further urged the Jharkhand government to address the students' grievances."The Jharkhand government must continue to hear these students out and resolve their issues immediately," he added.The JPSC and JSSC examinations have been at the centre of protests by aspirants over alleged irregularities. Separately, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) has registered an Enforcement Case Information Report under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act in connection with alleged irregularities in JPSC examinations.
Article Summary: Congress leader Sam Pitroda criticises government's use of lathis, tear gas and water cannons as protests enter 18th day. Protesters are demanding cancellation of JSSC-Combined Graduate Level (CGL) examination, a CBI probe into alleged irregularities and reforms in the recruitment process. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi also condemned the police action.

Article Title: 'At no cost' will Mann complete tenure: Congress' Warring predicts AAP govt collapse in Punjab
Article Text:
Congress Warring predicts AAP govt collapse in Punjab (PTI photo)

NEW DELHI: Punjab Congress president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring took a dig at chief minister Bhagwant Mann , saying the ongoing Vidhan Sabha session could be his last. The sharp jibe at Punjab CM came months prior to Punjab's assembly elections set for early next year.Warring also claimed that the Aam Aadmi Party government could soon lose its majority because of growing discontent among its MLAs.While bidding farewell to Mann, Warring said the chief minister would "at no cost" complete his tenure. He claimed that even if the Punjab assembly elections are held as scheduled in February 2027, Mann would not remain chief minister until then."The Aam Aadmi Party is likely to implode very soon as the government is losing its majority. Many MLAs are just waiting for the opportune moment, which is not very far," he said.Warring claimed that most AAP MLAs were "completely alienated and disillusioned" with their own government. "For four and a half years, they have felt suffocated and they are now waiting for the breather," he said.The Punjab Congress chief alleged that despite receiving a strong mandate, the AAP government had failed both the people of Punjab and its own MLAs."Mann has proved to be the worst ever chief minister Punjab had, for which they will never forgive him," he said.Warring also criticised CM Mann for continuing to rely on his image as a comedian after becoming chief minister.He said Mann had failed to understand that his role had changed after taking charge of the state."Unfortunately, Mann could not make the difference that his stage had changed and he was no longer required to survive through narrating jokes and anecdotes. People of Punjab had not elected you to make them laugh, for that they already had enough of your comedy," he said.The PCC president said people had voted for Mann expecting "badlaav" (change), but alleged that he had instead given up his authority to "outsiders" to protect his position as chief minister."Instead, you surrendered all your authority to outsiders while guarding your chief ministerial chair, for which you sacrificed the interests of Punjab. History will never forgive you for that," Warring warned CM Mann.Earlier, on August 5, Warring said he wanted to contest the 2027 assembly election against Mann and urged the Congress leadership to field him from Mann's constituency.Addressing a gathering in Faridkot, Warring said the final decision would be taken by Congress leaders Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi."While Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge have to make a decision. I am not in a position to do that. Either don't field me at all, or if you do field me, field me against Bhagwant Mann. I will contest," he said.The remarks come as political parties prepare for the 2027 Punjab assembly elections. The AAP, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) have already started preparations for the polls.The AAP won the 2022 Punjab assembly elections with a strong majority, forming its first government in the state and ending the Congress' tenure in power.
Article Summary: Punjab Congress president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring took a dig at chief minister Bhagwant Mann. He said the ongoing Vidhan Sabha session could be his last. The sharp jibe at Punjab CM came months prior to Punjab's assembly elections set for early next year.

Article Title: Govt condemns vandalism of Indian embassy in Slovenia
Article Text:
Ministry of external affairs said in an official statement that under the Vienna Convention, diplomatic premises are inviolable and must be protected.

NEW DELHI: Condemning the defacement of Indian embassy premises in Slovenia by Khalistan separatists, the govt urged law enforcement authorities elsewhere too to take note of the hateful propaganda and disinformation being spread by such groups.Ministry of external affairs said in an official statement that under the Vienna Convention, diplomatic premises are inviolable and must be protected."We have taken up the matter strongly with Slovenian authorities, both in New Delhi and in Ljubljana so that the perpetrators behind such reprehensible acts are held accountable to the full extent of the law," it said."We also call upon law enforcement authorities elsewhere to take note of the hateful propaganda and disinformation being spread by such groups," it added.In recent years, Indian diplomatic missions have been targeted, vandalised, or defaced with pro-Khalistan slogans and flags in many other countries, including Australia, Canada, UK and the US.
Article Summary: Ministry of external affairs said in an official statement that under the Vienna Convention, diplomatic premises are inviolable and must be protected. In recent years, Indian diplomatic missions have been targeted, vandalised, or defaced with pro-Khalistan slogans and flags in many other countries.

Article Title: India move will muddle border talks: China
Article Text:
State-run Global Times quoted Chinese experts as saying India’s move would not alter the legal status of the disputed territory but could complicate future boundary negotiations.

GUWAHATI: China has hit back sharply at India for assigning standard names to 27 geographical locations in Arunachal Pradesh, with the state-run Global Times claiming these areas are in China's 'Zangnan' region - Beijing's term for Arunachal Pradesh and adjoining areas that it claims as part of Tibet Autonomous part.The daily reiterated that Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said at a routine press briefing on April 14 that the Zangnan region is China's territory and "China does not recognise the so-called 'Arunachal Pradesh' illegally set up by India. It is fully within China's sovereign rights for the Chinese govt to issue standard names for some of the places in Zangnan."The reaction came three days after India's Survey of India updated its official map to identify 21 land areas, four passes, a high-altitude glacial lake and a 1962 war hero monument in Arunachal Pradesh, which govt said was an exercise to ensure the "correct identification" of places and enhance public awareness of their geographical and historical significance.Global Times reported on Sunday night that the mapping by India came shortly after the 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on China-India Border Affairs (WMCC), held on Aug 6 in New Delhi, where officials from both sides discussed issues including boundary delimitation, border management and control, mechanism building and cross-border cooperation."India's latest move is essentially an attempt to reinforce its claims over disputed territory and counter China's sovereignty position," Guo Xuetang, a professor at Shanghai International Studies University, said.The latest "war of names" adds another layer to an already complex border dispute, even as both sides seek to keep military and diplomatic channels open.
Article Summary: India's Survey of India updated its official map to identify 21 land areas, four passes, a high-altitude glacial lake and a 1962 war hero monument. China has hit back sharply at India for assigning standard names to 27 geographical locations in Arunachal Pradesh. State-run Global Times claims these areas are in China's 'Zangnan' region.

Article Title: Jharkhand protest: Police defend ‘mild force’, to scan CCTV for miscreants - key points
Article Text:
The students have been protesting against alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC recruitment examinations.

Police to analyse CCTV footage

DC says stone was thrown at jawan

NEW DELHI: Police will examine CCTV footage to identify people they allege disrupted a largely peaceful student protest in Ranchi on Monday, as top officials defended the use of “mild” and “minimum” force to disperse job aspirants marching towards the Jharkhand Assembly.The agitation, which entered its 17th day, saw police use water cannons, tear gas and lathicharge during the ‘Vidhan Sabha Gherao’ march by students protesting alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).While police said protesters refused repeated requests to clear the route and alleged that some people damaged barricades, pelted stones and tried to stop vehicles, student protesters accused police of using force without warning. An injured protester claimed that at least 100 young men were beaten during the lathicharge.Ranchi SSP Rakesh Ranjan said police would examine CCTV footage from the protest to identify those allegedly responsible for disrupting the demonstration."Police will analyse CCTV footage to identify anti-social elements who disrupted the peaceful students' protest," Rakesh Ranjan told reporters.Ranjan said 14 police personnel were injured during Monday’s protest, including one who suffered a major injury. According to him, police used only the minimum force required to bring the situation under control."We had previously communicated--and it was agreed--that the siege of the Legislative Assembly complex would be entirely peaceful. The police exercised considerable restraint, and we allowed the students to proceed gradually as far as they wished to go. We employed the minimum amount of force necessary based on the unfolding situation, and as a result, the current situation is peaceful," SSP Ranjan said in the joint presser.He alleged that some protesters repeatedly tried to create a disturbance, including attempts to stop vehicles and objects being thrown at them."The police used minimal force; we allowed the protesters to do whatever they wished to do all day long. We made every effort to reason with them and persuade them gently. There were some individuals who did not listen and repeatedly tried to create a ruckus. Attempts were made to stop passing vehicles--including those of officials--and objects like shoes and slippers were hurled at them," Ranchi SSP added.Ranchi Deputy Commissioner Manjunath Bhajantri also defended the police action, saying the force had exercised restraint throughout the protest and intervened only after a police personnel was allegedly put in danger."On July 24, some students and student leaders launched an indefinite protest. Since it had started without permission--and given the upcoming Durand Cup and Tribal Festival--a request was made for them to relocate; they subsequently moved to Jaipal Singh Stadium on July 28," DC Bhajantri said.He said the protest continued at the stadium while talks were held between student representatives and a state government committee. The agitation later intensified after student organisations called for a siege of the Assembly."Throughout this, our police force demonstrated restraint and strove to avoid using force. Amidst this, certain anti-social elements attempted to provoke the police and officials; a stone was thrown at a jawan, and another jawan was being crushed by the crowd, placing his life in danger. Consequently, the police used mild force to rescue the jawan," the DC said.Bhajantri said protesters had also refused repeated appeals by police and magistrates to clear a route towards the Assembly."Despite repeated requests from the police and magistrates to clear a path, the protesters refused to do so; therefore, mild force was used to remove them and normalise the situation," he said.The DC also called for those allegedly attempting to disturb the peace to be identified."I urge that the anti-social elements who are joining in to incite such situations be identified. The police will also take further action to identify them," he said.
Article Summary: Police use water cannons, tear gas and lathicharge during the ‘Vidhan Sabha Gherao’ march by students. Students are protesting alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) Ranchi Deputy Commissioner Manjunath Bhajantri says force exercised restraint throughout the protest.

Article Title: 'Our mother tongue is as pure as our mother': Vijay moves Tamil anthem resolution; DMK, AIADMK back it
Article Text:
Tamil Thai Vazhthu is an invocation to Mother Tamil from Manonmaniam, a play written by Manonmaniam Sundaranar in 1891. (Photo: PTI)

What does the resolution say?

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday moved a government resolution in the assembly making the rendition of Tamil Thai Vazhthu, the state song, mandatory at the beginning of official programmes across the state.Moving the resolution in the state assembly, Vijay said his Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam government would not compromise on Tamil Nadu's linguistic and cultural rights and urged legislators to set aside political differences in supporting the measure."Our mother tongue is as pure as our mother," Vijay said in an emotive speech, adding that, "Tamil is not only a language but also our life and emotions.""Tamil means pride, Tamil means power. The moment you say 'Tamil', the entire Tamil Nadu will come together and stand as one," he said."Tamil Thai Vazhthu must hold the first place in Tamil Nadu. Giving first place to Tamil Thaai Vaazhthu is our state right," he noted."Saying that Tamil Thai Vazhthu should be sung first does not need to become a political debate," the Tamil nadu CM said, appealing to members across party lines to support the resolution.Under the resolution, Tamil Thai Vazhthu will be sung first at programmes held by educational institutions, universities, government offices, public sector undertakings and other public institutions in Tamil Nadu.The resolution received support from both DMK and AIADMK legislators, with members backing the government's move to mandate the singing of the state song at official functions.The move comes amid a recent advisory from the Union home ministry asking states and Union territories to comply with its January 28 directive on playing Vande Mataram before the National Anthem at official events.It also comes against the backdrop of a July 9 communication from the ministry of home affairs regarding the singing of state songs at official programmes.The resolution describes Tamil Thai Vazhthu as an expression of respect for the Tamil language and culture and links its mandatory rendition to the linguistic and cultural rights guaranteed under the Constitution."Therefore, this House ( Tamil Nadu Assembly ) emphasises that "Tamil Thai Vazhthu" is an expression of respect for the Tamil language and Tamil culture. In accordance with the linguistic and cultural rights guaranteed by the Constitution of India, and with a view to preserving the Cultural identity of Tamil Nadu, the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly unanimously resolves that "Tamil Thai Vazhthu" shall be mandatorily sung first, before the commencement of programmes held by all Educational Institutions, Universities, Government Offices, Public Sector Undertakings and other Public Institutions in Tamil Nadu," the resolution said.The resolution also notes that Tamil is one of the world's oldest classical languages and describes Tamil civilisation as one of the world's oldest cultural traditions.Tamil Nadu had first directed that Tamil Thai Vazhthu be sung at the beginning of official functions through a government order issued on November 23, 1970.The state government formally accorded the song the status of the state song on December 12, 2021, making its rendition mandatory at official programmes and institutions across the state.Tamil Thai Vazhthu is an invocation to Mother Tamil from Manonmaniam, a play written by Manonmaniam Sundaranar in 1891.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday moved a government resolution in the assembly making the rendition of Tamil Thai Vazhthu, the state song, mandatory at the beginning of official programmes across the state. Vijay said his Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam government would not compromise on Tamil Nadu's linguistic and cultural rights.

Article Title: Government may be going slow on FCRA to woo DMK, NCP(SP) for delimitation
Article Text:
The Bill was introduced in Lok Sabha on March 25 but has not been taken up for discussion yet, amid fierce protest from opposition parties and minority groups, especially Christian bodies

Government may prefer full-fledged debate on FCRA to address criticism against the bill

NEW DELHI: The passage of FCRA amendment bill is not in Lok Sabha's agenda for Monday as Parliament's monsoon session enters its last week, giving rise to the view that government may be going slow on the contentious piece of legislation to sweeten the deal for parties such as DMK and NCP(SP), which are opposed to its provisions and are being seen by the governing alliance as prospective backers for its delimitation exercise.Sources said the meeting of LS's business advisory committee, where upcoming agenda items are finalised, on Monday will give more clarity as a schedule for discussion on the bill should be fixed if it has to be taken up for passage in the remaining four days of Parliament's monsoon session ending on Aug 13. Monday's agenda includes the introduction of four bills but makes no mention of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill.The Bill was introduced in Lok Sabha on March 25 but has not been taken up for discussion yet, amid fierce protest from opposition parties and minority groups, especially Christian bodies.Christian groups, which are a major recipient of foreign funding, have decried the proposed amendments, saying it threatens their charitable works and will allow the government to seize their assets if their FCRA licence is withdrawn or not renewed.What has, though, made things politically trickier for the BJP is the support extended by DMK president M K Stalin to the demand of a delegation representing churches of different denominations in their meeting with home minister Amit Shah that the bill be either withdrawn or sent to a joint parliamentary committee for scrutiny.With the government looking to assuage DMK’s concerns to get it on board before it makes a fresh bid for Parliament’s nod for its delimitation exercise, coupled with implementation of the women’s reservation law from 2029, it may not like to put the regional party on the defensive by bringing up the FCRA bill, some MPs said.Supriya Sule of NCP SP, another party being eyed by the government as a probable supporter for the amendment bill, has also opposed the FCRA bill.Mizoram CM Lalduhoma had told the media after joining a group of Church bodies from his state for a meeting with Amit Shah on Thursday that he was told that a debate on the bill is expected to be held on Aug 12.The continuing impasse in Parliament due to the opposition’s protests has added uncertainty as the government will prefer a full-fledged debate so that the home ministry could address the criticism around the bill.
Article Summary: Government may prefer full-fledged debate on FCRA to address criticism against the bill. Monday's agenda includes introduction of four bills but makes no mention of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill. Christian groups, which are a major recipient of foreign funding, have decried the proposed amendments.

Article Title: Jharkhand assembly gherao: Security stepped up with 750m curbs, barbed-wire barricades
Article Text:
Jharkhand Police imposed prohibitory orders around the Assembly and strengthened security across the city as students marched against alleged recruitment exam irregularities.

March to begin at 10:30 am

Prohibitory orders around Assembly

Barricades and barbed wire deployed

Security stepped up across Ranchi

Schools to remain closed

Ranchi administration warns against aggressive protests

BJP alleges Aditya Sahu placed under house arrest

Jamshedpur also under restrictions

Students allege police stopping protesters from reaching Ranchi

Students asked to maintain peace

Police clarifies viral ‘pellet gun’ video

NEW DELHI: Ranchi is under heightened security on Monday as protesting students prepare to march to the Jharkhand Vidhan Sabha over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. The students, who have been agitating for 16 days, have announced a ‘Vidhan Sabha March’ despite the state government saying it has accepted 98 per cent of their demands.The march is scheduled to begin between 10:30 and 11 am, with students gathering at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium from 9 am, according to student leader Ravindra Paswan. He urged protesters to remain peaceful and follow constitutional norms.Speaking to ANI, Paswan said, "A march to the Vidhan Sabha and a gherao will be conducted in a peaceful and constitutional manner. Students started gathering there at 9:00 AM. The march will commence between 10:30 and 11:00 AM. I urge all students and the general public to maintain peace and adhere to constitutional norms. Since we students are leading this movement, we must demonstrate that we are disciplined and educated. Students from every district of Jharkhand are arriving for today's protest; there will be a massive turnout."A prohibitory order has been imposed within a 750-metre radius of the Jharkhand Vidhan Sabha from August 6 to 12.The restrictions will remain in force from 6 am to 10 pm each day.Police have put up barricades around the Assembly premises, with barbed wire installed at parts of the protest route to prevent demonstrators from reaching restricted areas.Ranchi SSP Rakesh Ranjan said that maintaining law and order during the march is everyone’s responsibility. "We do not want a blot on the career of any student due to disruption of law and order. Barricades have been put in place at major points with the deployment of adequate police force across the city," the SSP said.The Jharkhand Police and district administration have made elaborate security arrangements across the city ahead of the students’ ‘Vidhan Sabha March’. The government said no student would be harassed during the protest.Most schools in Ranchi will remain closed on Monday in view of the planned march, with authorities taking precautionary measures ahead of the expected turnout.The Ranchi district administration appealed to agitating students to refrain from aggressive demonstrations and cautioned against violence or illegal activities during the march to the Assembly.BJP leader Amar Bauri alleged that the party’s state unit president Aditya Sahu had been “put under house arrest” ahead of Monday’s protest.A prohibitory order was imposed in Jamshedpur from Sunday midnight in view of the protest march in Ranchi, according to an official statement.Protesters alleged that hundreds of students travelling to Ranchi from different parts of Jharkhand were being stopped by police forcefully.Student leader Ravindra Paswan urged protesters to remain peaceful and follow constitutional norms during the march, which is scheduled to begin between 10:30 and 11 am.Ranchi City SP Paras Rana addressed concerns over a viral video that appeared to show a pellet gun, clarifying that the weapon was actually a paintball gun. "If a pellet gun is being carried, it is strictly for emergency situations. Article Text:

NEW DELHIi: Supreme Court on Monday admitted a petition challenging acquittal of Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim , who is serving a 20-year sentence for sexually assaulting two female disciples, in the 2002 murder of Sirsa-based journalist Ram Chander Chhatrapati.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana overruled protests by Rahim’s counsel R Basant that it was a case of acquittal and that the state had not filed any appeal against the acquittal.“This matter requires consideration. It is a reversal of conviction (recorded by the trial court). It is not an acquittal affirmed by HC. We are equally conscious that the state (CBI) will not appeal against the acquittal,” it said. The trial court had convicted Rahim and sentenced him to life imprisonment in Jan 2019.Admitting a petition by Arindam Chhatrapati, the complainant and son of the murdered journalist, the bench requisitioned the trial court records, including witness statements, for scrutiny. It posted final hearing of the matter in Nov last week.Basant said HC had recorded a categorical finding that the key witness could not be believed at all.“We will examine the special circumstances attending to the examination of the key witness and whether the appreciation of his evidence is appropriate,” responded the bench.The appellant said, “Despite affirming the categorical findings of the trial court on the existence of a conspiracy for the commission of Chhatrapati’s murder and upholding the convictions of the three co-accused under Section 120-B IPC read with Section 302 IPC, HC incorrectly arrived at a conclusion that participation of Baba Gurmeet Singh in the conspiracy is not proved.”Finding lapses in the local police probe, Punjab and Haryana HC had in Nov 2003, almost a year after the murder, transferred the investigations to the CBI. The key witness, referred to by the SC, is the ex-driver of Rahim.
Article Summary: Supreme Court on Monday admitted a petition challenging acquittal of Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim. Rahim is serving a 20-year sentence for sexually assaulting two female disciples. The trial court had convicted Rahim and sentenced him to life imprisonment in Jan 2019.

Article Title: Government says LoP Rahul Gandhi to sit per the table of precedence during Independence Day
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Defence secretary RK Singh on Monday said leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has been invited to the Independence Day celebrations at the Red Fort on August 15 and will be seated immediately after the Union Cabinet ministers."Leader of opposition has been invited, and his seating would be as per the Table of Precedence, which is exactly after Cabinet ministers," Singh told news agency ANI.In 2024, Rahul Gandhi's seating arrangement during the Independence Day celebrations had triggered a row after the Congress criticised the government for giving him a seat in the "fifth row" and calling the move a display of "pettiness" and a disregard for democratic norms. Officials from the ministry of defence, which organises the event, clarified that the 5th row seating arrangement for LoP was necessiated because of adjustment of 4 Olympic medalist in each row along with the ministers after first two rows.Earlier this year, the Congress had again accused the Centre of violating established protocol and undermining democratic decorum after Rahul Gandhi and Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge were seated in the third row during the Republic Day celebrations.However, the defence ministry refuted the charge and stated that the seating arrangements were done as per the "Table of Precedence".According to the Warrant of Precedence issued by the President's secretariat, seating arrangements at state and ceremonial occasions are decided based on constitutional rank and office, and not political affiliation. The Table of Precedence is a protocol list that applies to state and ceremonial occasions, including national events such as Republic Day celebrations, and has no application to the day-to-day functioning of the government.As per this, the leader of opposition in Lok Sabha has a rank equivalent to that of a Cabinet minister.

Police are also trying to establish how the drugs were procured and dispatched to Ganderbal through the courier.“We are also investigating whether the drugs were originally procured in the Valley and then dispatched to Kanpur, just to be couriered back to the poultry farm owner,” police said.

NEW DELHI: Union minister JP Nadda on Monday countered leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi , refuting his allegations that the government ordered the Delhi police to fire upon students protesting against the NEET paper leak on July 20.During a press conference, the Union minister accused Rahul of "shifting goalposts" to prevent Parliament from functioning."Rahul Gandhi keeps shifting the goalposts, both in Parliament and in the narrative, on a daily basis. His objective is not to engage in dialogue but to spread chaos. Initially, at the start of the session, he demanded a discussion on NEET. Today, when it was decided that the Jantar Mantar issue would indeed be discussed, he began misleading the people and the country by claiming that shots were fired at Jantar Mantar, when, in fact, no such incident occurred," he added.Nadda's remarks came hours after the Congress leader, during a press conference, reiterated his three demands, which he termed as "non-negotiables", to break the Parliament deadlock.The Congress leader demanded that Union home minister Amit Shah tell Parliament who ordered firing against students during the NEET paper leak protest. He said, apart from Shah's statement, PM Modi should apologise for what happened and called for accountability over the alleged donation theft in Ayodhya's Ram Mandir."The question was always that Amit Shah has to make it clear who authorised the shooting of our youngsters in Delhi. NEW DELHI: Thousands of job aspirants protesting alleged irregularities in Jharkhand recruitment examinations clashed with security forces on Monday after breaching multiple barricades and attempting to reach the state assembly. Police used water cannons, fired tear gas shells and carried out a lathi-charge as protesters moved towards the assembly premises.The protest, now in its 17th day, has intensified despite several rounds of talks between the government and demonstrators.The agitators are demanding cancellation of several recruitment exams, reforms in the JPSC and JSSC, and an independent probe into alleged irregularities."I extend my heartfelt thanks to all the officials and personnel of the administration and police for handling the situation during today's student movement with restraint, sensitivity, and complete responsibility. My dear young companions, you have raised your voice for your demands in a peaceful manner. In a democracy, it is your right to express your views, and it is the government's responsibility to respect your voice. The government has heard you. Our senior ministers have been in constant dialogue with you, and I assure you that action will be taken on your demands with utmost seriousness and sensitivity. In the past few days, you have seen that the government has spared no one, no matter who the guilty party is.Our clear objective is to eliminate such shortcomings in the system so that no student has to face trouble in the future," he said."We want to make the examination system more transparent, technology-enabled, secure, and accountable. Your participation in this change is the most important. Our effort is that Jharkhand should not just discuss problems, but set a new example of solutions from here. I also understand that amidst your peaceful movement, some people from the opposition have tried to spoil the atmosphere and mislead students for political gain. I appeal to all of you not to fall into the trap of any such political narrative. You are the future of Jharkhand. It is not about ignoring your voice, but listening to it and resolving your problems—that is our responsibility. I will reiterate my point: let us resolve this issue together through dialogue and trust," he added.Some protesters breached barricades and entered the Jharkhand assembly premises. Police used water cannons and fired several rounds of tear gas when the protesters reached the final barricade near Jagannathpur Temple, around 200 metres from the assembly.Despite the security action, a section of protesters managed to symbolically enter the assembly premises. Police also resorted to a lathi-charge after the demonstrators attempted to move forward.Several protesters claimed they were injured, including female students. The assembly was adjourned for the day in the afternoon.Four policemen were injured after protesters allegedly pelted stones at security personnel during a march towards the Jharkhand assembly in Ranchi, city SP Paras Rana said.Moreover, JLKM leader Devendra Mahto was hospitalised after his health deteriorated during a nine-day hunger strike.The BJP has called for a Jharkhand bandh on Tuesday in protest against the alleged police atrocities and lathi-charge on students demonstrating over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations.The march began around 10.30am from outside the old assembly building and coincided with chief minister Hemant Soren's 51st birthday.Jharkhand CID arrested former JPSC chairperson L Khiangte in connection with alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations, taking the total number of arrests in the case to 20.Khiangte, a 1988-batch IAS officer, was appointed JPSC chairperson in February last year after retiring as the state's chief secretary. He resigned from the post on July 22, saying he had voluntarily stepped down to facilitate an impartial investigation.The former JPSC chief had been questioned four times since July 28. His arrest came a day after all three JPSC members — Ajeeta Bhattacharya, Anima Hansda and Jamal Ahmad — resigned after being summoned by the CID for questioning.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi criticised the use of force against the protesting students, saying they had a right to peaceful protest."The use of force against students protesting in Jharkhand is wrong," Gandhi said, adding that only dialogue could resolve the issue. He urged the state government to continue listening to the protesters and resolve their concerns immediately.The JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, which is spearheading the agitation, has demanded comprehensive reforms in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission.The protesters are seeking cancellation of several recruitment examinations, including the 14th JPSC Civil Services Examination, and an independent probe by either the CBI or a panel of retired High Court judges from outside the state.They said the government had agreed to cancel only three of the 13 examinations they want scrapped.State minister Sudivya Kumar alleged that the agitation had moved beyond a students' movement and was being driven by the BJP's political agenda. He claimed the government had already fulfilled 95% of the protesters' demands.BJP Yuva Morcha state president Shashank Raj, however, called the police action a "black day for democracy" and urged chief minister Hemant Soren not to be "insensitive" towards the students' demands.
Article Summary: Thousands of job aspirants protesting alleged irregularities in Jharkhand recruitment examinations clash with security forces. The protest, now in its 17th day, has intensified despite several rounds of talks between the government and demonstrators.

A court in Thiruvananthapuram on Monday granted bail to right-wing political commentator T G Mohandas, who was arrested over alleged remarks in a YouTube video concerning a student protest in New Delhi linked to the NEET paper leak.Mohandas was produced before the Thiruvananthapuram Additional Chief Judicial First Class Magistrate Court for remand proceedings. Judge Mithun Gopi G S granted him bail after hearing arguments from both sides.Police had taken Mohandas into custody from his residence in Mattancherry, Kochi, on Sunday evening. His arrest was formally recorded on Monday.The case has been registered under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the Information Technology Act and the Kerala Police Act. The Thiruvananthapuram Cyber Police also informed the court that additional charges had been added for allegedly using words, sounds, gestures or objects intended to insult a woman's modesty, as well as for criminal intimidation involving severe threats.The prosecution asked the court to allow Mohandas to remain in custody for further investigation. It argued that he was an influential person who could potentially influence witnesses or interfere with evidence if released.His defence opposed the request, citing his age and health condition. His lawyer also argued that all the offences invoked against him were bailable.After considering the submissions, the court granted Mohandas bail. It directed him to appear before the investigating officer for three days as part of the ongoing probe and to appear before police whenever required.The court also ordered him not to repeat a similar offence while he remains on bail.The case stems from a complaint against videos posted on Mohandas' YouTube channel, 'Pathrika'. The complaint alleged that the videos were capable of disturbing public order and creating fear and unrest.In one of the videos, Mohandas allegedly said the Delhi students' protest "could lead to incidents of gang rape" and claimed that there would be no complaints because "those attending the protest like rape and there are girls who enjoy being raped".He further claimed that although some people would be killed or permanently injured, the situation would be brought under control within hours and the bodies shifted to hospitals.

Article Title: Watch: Jharkhand students carry Mahto as police lathicharge, use water cannons, tear gas during march

Police on Monday used water cannons, tear gas and resorted to a lathi charge as thousands of students protesting alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations marched towards the Jharkhand Assembly in Ranchi. The protesters attempted to breach multiple layers of barricades as they advanced towards the Assembly.At least three people, including two protesters and a Jharkhand Armed Police (JAP) personnel, were injured during the confrontation, according to officials. The protesters were taking part in the ‘Vidhan Sabha Gherao’ march organised by the JPSC-JSSC Reform Morcha.Several videos surfaced online showing protesters advancing towards the Assembly despite multiple layers of barricading and heightened security as the Monsoon Session of the Jharkhand Assembly remained underway. Videos also showed police using water cannons against the protesters, some of whom were seen dancing and raising slogans as they faced the water jets.Police deployed water cannons as the crowd pushed through successive barricades before resorting to a lathi charge to prevent further movement.Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM) leader Devendra Nath Mahto also joined the march and was seen being carried by protesters as they moved towards the Assembly.Mahto has been on a hunger strike at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, the main protest site, for the past nine days.Carrying a portrait of former Jharkhand chief minister Shibu Soren, Mahto said, “Despite being on hunger strike, the barbed wires will not be able to stop us. I came here in an ambulance. The government will have to listen to us.”Mahto said protesters had already crossed three layers of barricading and questioned the government's response to the agitation.“I am no God or messiah; I am a common man. There will be no change in my personal life. But the barbed wires hurt more than the hunger strike. Students crossed three layers of barricading. Why does the government want anarchy and not agree to students' demands?” he said.He also urged chief minister Hemant Soren not to allow the situation to escalate.“Today it's CM Hemant Soren's birthday, and he should not take such a step where some unfortunate events like at the Jantar Mantar take place here. Do not do anything that causes someone to bleed or get injured and makes the crowd even more agitated,” Mahto said.“Arrest is a legal process, but there should be no bloodshed. If the government does not agree to the demands, it will be remembered as the one which killed democracy. I will not end the fast,” he added.Vikram Kumar, a student protester injured in the lathi charge, alleged that police action came without provocation.“Hemant Soren ji, you should not have done this. We were protesting peacefully. We did not even hurl any abuses. Suddenly, the police launched a lathi charge. This is not good,” Kumar said.The protesters are demanding cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination, a CBI probe into alleged irregularities and reforms to the recruitment process.The agitation coincided with the Enforcement Directorate (ED) registering an Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR) under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) in connection with alleged irregularities in examinations conducted by the JPSC.

Referring to the reported use of force, he questioned how the Modi government responds to young people demanding answers about their future.He wrote in his post on X: "Pellet guns, Nail-studded lathis, tear gas fired at students who were peacefully asking questions about their own future. And we will not stop fighting until he is held accountable."In his column, Rahul recalled meeting students who were injured during the protests and questioned the Centre's handling of the incident. He argued that power in the government is highly "centralised" and pointed out that the Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force (RAF), deployed at Jantar Mantar on July 20, report to Amit Shah-led Union home ministry.He presented two possibilities: either Shah "authorised" the police action or he had "no idea that it was taking place"."The Narendra Modi government prides itself on its centralised control. Nothing moves without their approval.""The violence happened in the heart of Delhi, barely 500 metres from Parliament. Both the security forces deployed, the Delhi Police and the Rapid Action Force (RAF), report directly to the home minister," he added.LoP in Lok Sabha said Shah's failure to address Parliament over the incident raises questions about his responsibility as Home Minister.He said, "There are only two possibilities. First, he authorised the attack on the students - in which case he is culpable. Second, he had no idea that it was taking place - which means that he is entirely incompetent. Either way, as Home Minister, what happened on that day is his responsibility, and he must resign.""Instead, his inaction proves that he approves of the attack on students. He has not ordered any inquiry or even issued a statement. He has refused to come to Parliament, and motions filed," the column read.The Congress and the INDIA bloc have repeatedly demanded a statement from Amit Shah in Parliament and have staged protests both inside and outside the House over the issue.On Monday, another Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi also demanded statement from Amit Shah in Parliament.Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju, however, has maintained that the Opposition cannot dictate which minister should come to Parliament and make a statement, saying the decision rests with the government.
Article Summary: Opposition leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi steps up his attack on the Centre. He takes direct aim at Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah. Article Title: Sourav Ganguly, wife Dona receive death threats; Kolkata Police begin probe
Article Text:
Sourav Ganguly (Image credit: X)

Threatening letters received over six months

Police track courier trail

Police examine possible motive

NEW DELHI: Former India captain Sourav Ganguly has approached the police after receiving several threatening letters over the past few months, including one that allegedly threatened to kill him and his wife, Dona Ganguly, news agency PTI reported.Ganguly, who is currently the president of the Cricket Association of Bengal (CAB), filed a written complaint at Thakurpukur Police Station in south Kolkata after his office received two letters on Monday, a senior police officer said.According to the police complaint filed by Ganguly's manager, the letters had allegedly been arriving in his name for around six months. They were initially not taken seriously.However, two letters received at his office on Monday reportedly contained explicit threats to kill Ganguly and his wife and harm people close to him.The police have now started an investigation to identify the sender and find out the motive behind the threats."We are taking the complaint seriously and have begun an investigation. We are examining the letters, their source and the courier trail to identify the person responsible," the officer said.The preliminary investigation suggests that the letters may have been sent through a courier service, allegedly by a person from Belgharia in North 24 Parganas district.Police are also examining the movement of the SIM card allegedly used by the sender and have contacted the courier agency to collect details about the consignments."We have spoken to the people from the courier service and tracked down one mobile number. We are trying to spot it," the officer said.Kolkata Police are now checking whether all the letters were sent by the same person. Investigators are also trying to establish the reason behind the alleged threats.The police are examining the contents of the letters, their source and the courier trail as part of the probe.
Article Summary: Former India captain Sourav Ganguly has approached the police after receiving several threatening letters over the past few months. One letter allegedly threatened to kill him and his wife, Dona Ganguly. The police have now started an investigation to identify the sender and find out the motive behind the threats.

Article Title: Jack Roney autopsy: ‘Two minutes underwater’ before former NC State coach’s shocking death at 39
Article Text:
Jack Roney autopsy: ‘Two minutes underwater’ before former NC State coach’s shocking death at 39

Jack Roney was doing underwater breathing exercises before the accident

Jack Roney left NC State swimming record and five children

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former North Carolina State swimming coach Jack Roney died at 39 on July 5 after what was described as a tragic accident. A newly reported autopsy account gives more detail about what happened at a community pool that evening. Roney had been doing underwater breathing exercises while swimming with his wife, Maresa, according to US Weekly. He went underwater for more than two minutes, came up for air and then went back under. His wife briefly stepped away to make a phone call. When she returned about five minutes later, she found him unresponsive in the water. Roney was taken to a hospital but could not be saved.The autopsy report said Roney was an avid swimmer and had been holding his breath underwater while at the pool with Maresa after dinner.According to the report: “Wife told medics her husband was an avid swimmer and on that evening, he had been doing some breathing exercises [and] holding his breath underwater.“Wife pulled him from the water and called 911… then began CPR. There were no concerns for suicide, substance abuse or foul play.“No trauma was noted. Law enforcement was reviewing footage of the incident. Due to the circumstances of the death, pathology at the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner was consulted and the case was accepted there for autopsy.”Emergency responders continued CPR as Roney was taken to the hospital. A separate medical examiner statement said he was in pulseless electrical activity when responders arrived and that resuscitation efforts continued for about an hour.The same statement said Roney “had a history of ADHD.” It also confirmed that he was last known to be alive on the evening of July 5, when he and Maresa went to their community pool after dinner.Roney was well known at NC State as both a swimmer and coach. He graduated from the university in 2009 and left the program as its record holder in the 200-yard breaststroke. That mark has since been broken. He later returned as a volunteer assistant coach and worked with the swimming program from 2014 to 2016.NC State Swimming & Diving announced his death on July 6, writing: “Our thoughts and prayers are with the Roney family during this difficult time. His impact on our program and community will be remembered.”Roney and Maresa had recently marked their 15th wedding anniversary. They had five children: Gunnar, Scout, Beau, Archer and Crew.His death came just weeks before his 40th birthday. Public reports initially gave few details about what had happened, with friends describing it only as a “tragic accident.” The new account provides a clearer picture of the events at the pool while leaving the family to mourn a sudden loss.
Article Summary: Former North Carolina State swimming coach Jack Roney died at 39 on July 5 after what was described as a tragic accident. A newly reported autopsy account gives more detail about what happened at a community pool that evening. Roney had been doing underwater breathing exercises while swimming with his wife, Maresa, according to US Weekly. He went underwater for more than two minutes, came up for air and then went back under.

Article Title: ‘A terrible mistake’: Trump warns FIFA against replacing Infantino amid growing revolt
Article Text:
File Pic: US President Donald Trump with FIFA president Gianni Infantino (AP Photo)

‘A terrible mistake’ if Infantino is replaced

‘A fundamental breach of trust’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump has thrown his support behind FIFA president Gianni Infantino as pressure continues to mount on the football governing body's chief, warning that replacing him would be a "terrible mistake".Trump's intervention comes at a time when Infantino is facing one of the biggest challenges to his leadership, with UEFA , CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) accusing him of a "fundamental breach of trust" over a proposal to sell an interest in future FIFA World Cup profits to private investors.Trump, however, pointed to the success of the recently concluded expanded 2026 World Cup and backed Infantino's continued leadership.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote: "FIFA would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing President Gianni Infantino. He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented. If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again! Thank you for your attention to this matter. President DJT".The strong endorsement comes just months before FIFA's presidential election in March next year, with Infantino facing growing questions over his leadership and the trust placed in him by member associations.The controversy erupted after Infantino announced the FIFA Forward Enterprise, which sought private involvement and investment in FIFA-related competitions, particularly the World Cup. The proposal triggered fierce opposition from several football associations and confederations.The plan was eventually withdrawn following the backlash. Infantino and FIFA general secretary Mattias Grafstrom apologised for the process, acknowledged that errors had been made and promised that they would not be repeated. FIFA also pledged to conduct a review, with its findings to be submitted to the FIFA Council at its next meeting.The withdrawal, however, did little to end the controversy. UEFA, CONCACAF and the AFC launched a stinging attack on Infantino, insisting that the issue went far beyond communication or procedural errors.In an open letter to the "football family" on Monday, the three confederations said the dispute was not about money, World Cup expansion or competition allocations, but about the integrity of football's governing structures."This is not about money," they said, arguing that FIFA's reserves should instead be responsibly distributed to strengthen investment in member associations.They accused FIFA of presenting the episode as a communication failure when, in their view, it represented a deeper leadership problem."FIFA's recent letter to its Vice-Presidents and 211 Member Associations acknowledges that mistakes were made in the process. It treats this as a failure of communication, when what football witnessed was a failure of judgment," the confederations said.They further described the attempt to sell an interest in the World Cup as "a profound failure of judgment" and "a fundamental breach of trust with the very institutions FIFA exists to serve."The three confederations also called for an independent third-party investigation rather than a FIFA-led review, while FIFA has defended Infantino against what it described as a "concerted and ongoing effort" to undermine his leadership.Infantino received backing from FIFA's management board following a meeting in Morocco last week and apologised over the process surrounding the World Cup proposal. UEFA, however, said the announcement "changes nothing" about its opposition.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump has thrown his support behind FIFA president Gianni Infantino. Trump warns that replacing him would be a "terrible mistake" FIFA has come under pressure over a proposal to sell an interest in future FIFA World Cup profits to private investors.

Article Title: A note, 5-star hotel, an affair: What led Bengaluru man to kill his 2 daughters
Article Text:
A 40-year-old man allegedly killed his two minor daughters before attempting suicide at a five-star hotel.

Father found injured after alleged killings

What happened inside the hotel?

Investigation under way





BENGALURU: A 40-year-old man allegedly killed his two minor daughters before attempting suicide at a five-star hotel near Kempegowda International Airport (KIA) in Bengaluru on Monday, police said.The girls, Shaik Zehara, 5, and Shaik Zoya, 10, were found dead inside a fourth-floor hotel room. Their father, S G Imran, was found unconscious with a cut to his throat and was taken to a private hospital, where he remains under treatment.Police said Imran, a resident of Bilalnagar near Nagavara Main Road in north Bengaluru, allegedly strangled his daughters before attempting suicide.A note recovered from the hotel room is suspected to have been written by Imran. It referred to a marital dispute and accused his wife of having an extra-marital affair.“I am fed up with life due to the extra-marital affair of my wife. I have evidence to prove her affair. She has hurt me. I am taking my daughters with me,” it read.Imran, who works as a manager with a private cab company, checked into the hotel at around 7.30pm on Sunday, police said.Hotel staff said he told them he was expecting a guest from Dubai after midnight.Imran did not check out the following afternoon. Housekeeping staff knocked on his door at around 12.30pm but received no response. They tried again at about 4.30pm, but there was still no response, police said.At around 5.30pm, the hotel manager opened the door using a duplicate key and found the two children lying dead near the bed. Imran was found near the sofa with his throat slit.Police alerted after hotel staff raise alarmThe three were rushed to a nearby private hospital, where doctors declared the two girls dead on arrival. Imran was admitted for treatment.Mithun Kumar GK, deputy commissioner of police, north-east division, said the hotel's security manager informed police about the incident in the evening.Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the deaths and the alleged marital dispute mentioned in the note.They are also examining the note recovered from the room and other evidence from the hotel as part of the investigation.
Article Summary: S G Imran, 40, allegedly killed his two minor daughters before attempting suicide at a five-star hotel in Bengaluru. The girls, Shaik Zehara, 5, and Shaik Zoya, 10, were found dead inside a fourth-floor hotel room. Their father was found unconscious with a cut to his throat and was taken to a private hospital where he remains under treatment.

Article Title: ​​Youths on indefinite hunger strike against CJP founder shifted to hospital

He, however, said the agitation would continue despite their hospitalisation.Following the duo’s hospitalisation, two new volunteers replaced them at the protest site, announcing that they would carry forward the hunger strike against CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke.Brahmabhatt and Pandya had earlier said they stood shoulder to shoulder with Dipke during the Jantar Mantar agitation in Delhi, but only people close to Dipke were invited to the core committee meeting. Article Title: 'Modi govt responsible': Akhilesh blames Centre as Jharkhand job protest turns violent
Article Text:
Akhilesh Yadav blamed the central government for rising unemployment and student unrest.





NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Monday accused the BJP-led Centre of failing to address unemployment and said the Central government was responsible for resentment by students and job aspirants in Jharkhand.Yadav said the Centre had a responsibility to create employment opportunities for young people in Jharkhand and claimed that any positive initiative by the central government would ultimately benefit the state as well."The real person responsible for unemployment and for putting the future of youngsters in the dark is the Modi government," Yadav said, while responding to questions on the ongoing protests in Jharkhand.His remarks came amid a prolonged agitation by job aspirants in Ranchi over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. The protests turned tense on Monday, with police using water cannons, tear gas and lathi-charge after demonstrators breached barricades near the Jharkhand assembly. Several protesters and four policemen were injured.Yadav also questioned the Centre over the alleged misappropriation of donations at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya and demanded answers from the government."Who will answer for the alleged theft of offerings to Lord Ram? It is not an ordinary matter. It concerns the faith of crores of people," he said.The SP leader, along with other Opposition MPs, participated in a protest at Makar Dwar in the Parliament complex over the alleged police action against student protesters on July 20 and the Ram Mandir donation controversy.The opposition has been demanding a statement from Union Home Minister Amit Shah on the police action against student protesters. The demand has contributed to repeated disruptions in Parliament, with the Monsoon Session scheduled to conclude on August 13.Yadav also criticised the BJP, accusing it of being a "land mafia" party and alleging that faith was being used in connection with land and property in Ayodhya.On the reported attack on former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee's convoy, Yadav condemned the incident and said the government was responsible for ensuring her security."It is very sad to see such an incident happening in a democracy. She is a senior leader and was the chief minister there, and then she was attacked. The kind of behaviour being seen is condemnable," he said.Yadav added that if the government was behind the incident, it would be "highly reprehensible", and said Banerjee should be provided adequate security.Meanwhile, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju accused the opposition of disrupting proceedings and said the government was ready for a detailed discussion on the student-related issues.Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla also appealed to political parties to cooperate in restoring the functioning of the House, urging members to allow Question Hour and discussions on key bills.
Article Summary: Akhilesh Yadav blames the central government for rising unemployment and student unrest. Yadav also questioned the Centre over the alleged misappropriation of donations at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya. The SP leader, along with other Opposition MPs, participated in a protest at Makar Dwar in the Parliament complex.

Article Title: ‘Rehearsed, well-practised, planted’: Court on allegations against Brij Bhushan
Article Text:
The judge found the allegations “strikingly similar”, made at the same time and at a common place, indicating “prior meticulous planning”.





NEW DELHI: A court, which last week acquitted former BJP MP and former Wrestling Federation of India president Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh for lack of evidence, held that the sexual harassment allegations against him were “rehearsed and well-practised as well as planted” and appeared to be part of a “deep conspiracy, which seems to be politically motivated”.Additional chief judicial magistrate Ashwani Panwar observed in the 239-page order, “The allegations appear to be imperfect to be true, seem rehearsed and well-practised as well as planted, more so when the complaints have been filed after a long period of time.”The court on Aug 3 acquitted Singh of “all charges” under IPC sections 354 (assault or criminal force to a woman to outrage her modesty), 354A (sexual harassment) and 506 (I) (criminal intimidation), and former WFI assistant secretary Vinod Tomar of charges under IPC 506 (I).The court cited material contradictions in the successive versions of the survivors, documentary evidence inconsistent with the alleged dates and circumstances, and mentioned evidence of tutoring.Among the discrepancies was an alleged incident during an Olympic qualifier in Mongolia. The incident was initially stated to have taken place in Turkiye in 2015, and subsequently in Mongolia in 2016, the court pointed out, holding it to be “not a mere variation in peripheral details”.It also noted that major allegations involving Asian Games in Jakarta and Tokyo Olympics were absent from earlier affidavits before the oversight committee. A prosecution witness also changed the date of an alleged WFI office incident from Sunday, when the office was closed, to Monday, which the court termed a “material improvement”. A witness’ claim of an incident during a warm-up on Feb 28, 2018, also contradicted the official event schedules.“No doubt, it is really very difficult for everyone, including the victim, to remember the name and details of every place where the tournaments were held. However, it’s not difficult but rather abnormal conduct to not to remember the place where incident of sexual harassment had occurred, that too, in full public view, in a restaurant, where many sportsperson, coaches, including the relatives of the victim, were present and the incident was repeated three-four times at the said place,” the verdict said.Another “unnatural” conduct, Panwar observed, was the survivors maintaining “cordial relations” with Singh for years after the alleged incidents, even inviting him to family functions and weddings. “It is understandable as alleged that Singh, being the then WFI president, could have spoiled their careers if they had made complaint against him; however, it is not at all understandable as to why cordial relations were maintained with him for years. ”The survivors even met higher authorities but failed to disclose the alleged acts, and, since no formal complaint or retaliation followed, the court concluded that it was “highly improbable that the alleged acts are true”.The judge also found the allegations “strikingly similar”, made at the same time and at a common place, indicating “prior meticulous planning”. “I have no hitch in saying that the version given by the (two) victims (who turned hostile) discredits the prosecution case completely and also shows that the entire allegations are false and fabricated, made collectively at the instance of (two other wrestlers) and the coaches of Mahadev Academy. .. in deep conspiracy, which seems to be motivated politically.”The court also questioned how the complaints were prepared, noting that before the dharna, no sexual harassment allegation or names of alleged survivors were mentioned. Subsequently, “selected” wrestlers came forward and “same/similar allegations were incorporated in the tailor-made formal complaints drafted in a fancy manner, with similar excessive decoration”. Of the five survivors, the two who turned hostile “categorically admitted that no sexual harassment acts were committed against them” and their statements were given under threat.
Article Summary: Former BJP MP and former Wrestling Federation of India president Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh acquitted. Court held that the sexual harassment allegations against him were “rehearsed and well-practised as well as planted” The judge found the allegations “strikingly similar”, made at the same time and at a common place.
